items.box:
VERIFICATION AUTOMATION

Opened by Andy, 2026-10-06: "i want to add a new goal, while keeping this one alive: goal/G8 Verification Automation". It came out of his review of rule/4: "when closing an item, verify only with the items red. the full harness runs only to get the 'Done' button for the current goal."

HIS WORDS, the source of every item:
- "why is the harness not automated? demonized?"
- "imagine this: an auto-agent, it is a server process, completely mechanical, it does all the verifying on it's own?"
- "that auto-agent only verifies, it takes all verification, run's a short loop on all active items, pulls automatically on status changes, and delivers, only reds, unless a specific red is marked as tolerated."
- "the desk can mechanically verify that the verifier is active, and only under those circumstances deny a verify-take to other agents."
- "is there a way an agent could 'signoff' so it wont take 10 minutes?"

WHAT IT KEEPS: a running tally of every test, each flip from red to green and back, and which files each item touched and by whom.

THE ITEMS, each holding its own rulings verbatim:
- G8.1 the dataset: verify.db, one row per test. Waits on nothing; the keystone.
- G8.2 the running modes: one deskVerify that knows where it runs; on an agent node only a gate before that agent's Done, on the desk node the record.
- G8.3 what deskVerify may do as an agent on the desk node.
- G8.4 idle-time chores.
- G8.5 changes the desk must gain, among them that Done waits on every grant, and signoff.
- G8.6 the short loop: the goal's suites between Go and Done.
- G8.7 tolerated reds: one question on the goal listing the reds outside it.
- G8.8 files touched per item: the list, its one grant, its verb item.files.add, and Delete kept out of the List. Waits on nothing.
- G8.9 test runs that cannot collide: free ports and one full run per host. Waits on nothing.

Dependencies are explicit only (rule/6): G8.1 before G8.2; G8.2 before G8.3 to G8.6; G8.8 and G8.9 before G8.6; G8.9 before G8.4; G8.6 before G8.7. Still in design.

items.title: deskVerify: the dataSet — verify.db, one row per test, and what identifies a test
items.box:
deskVerify: THE DATASET

Andy's design, 2026-10-06. verify.db on every node deskVerify runs on. A row per test: suite, title, outcome, commit, dirty tree, UTC time. Secondary indexes on commit, outcome and dirty tree.

THE KEY is the suite plus the title as written in it. A failing assertion carries the same title as its passing one, its runtime detail beside the title and not inside it, or a change of outcome cannot be followed.

THE DIRTY TREE is the files modified against the commit last pulled, sorted, empty when clean, so a result measured on a dirty tree is never taken for one measured at a commit.

ROWS. A record is written when that test has none yet, or when its outcome changes, carrying the commit and time of that change; every run and commit in between is implicit. Runs are not stored at all. An outcome is red or green, nothing else. A test its suite never reached reports nothing, writes nothing, and its last state stands.

WHO SENDS IT is testSupport, the one place every check and fail already passes through. A suite deskVerify launched gets a port as a named argument and posts one record per assertion to deskVerify's loopback api, as it happens; a suite run by hand gets no port, sends nothing, and behaves as today. A record carries suite, title and outcome, since deskVerify launched the run and stamps the commit, dirty tree and time itself. The send is not waited on, those two calls being synchronous, and the suite waits once as it exits so the last records land.

DECIDED, not to be reopened: records are never sent together. Andy, 2026-10-06, after an earlier design had held them back: more complicated, saves little time, and risks overflowing MAX_PAYLOAD eventually. A later session that finds this slow does not get to group them. One record is about 136 bytes against a 22528 limit.

MEASURED IN THE TREE at 9ece24a8, what the above rests on:
- 362 suites, 4291 titled assertions, one title repeated in the whole harness (natterIntrinsic.js): suite plus title is unique.
- 4181 of 4780 failure sentences are built from runtime values, so the red and green of one assertion share no key today.
- The printed number counts passes and failures apart, so it changes when a test flips and cannot be the key.
- liveRelay.js reads its first positional argument as a relay address, hence a named port.

WHERE IT LIVES AND WHAT RECEIVES IT, his, 2026-10-06: "verify.db lives in deskVerify’s process folder and is .gitignored", and the records arrive by its own verb, "the verb \"record\" that supplies candidates for the database". So the history is per node and never travels in git, which the tree makes necessary: a tracked database would land in every clone, and the ignored relay-state folder would lose it on a fresh one. The verb belongs to deskVerify, not to the node, so it crosses no interface boundary.

THE NODE'S PORT, his, 2026-10-09: "THE hosting nodes port is automatically delivered to EVERY appServer automatically!!!!!!!! DO NOT RE-INVENT this mechanism!!!!" It is spirit.core.node.const.SPIRIT_PORT, which js/appServer.js sets from the node's relay-state/environment.json, and process/js/deskUnsloth reads. So deskVerify learns its node's port from that constant and nothing else; a suite it launches is not an app server and is told the same value as --verify-port, so a suite run by hand still posts nothing.

deskVerify: THE RUNNING MODES

Andy's design, 2026-10-06, extracted from the goal at his word. Blocked by goal/G8.1, since what a node records is settled before where it may record it.

THE THREE CASES. deskVerify runs on every node and keeps the same records in the same shape everywhere; only its standing and its work differ.
- THE DESK NODE, his work box. Authoritative: it reaches the desk on loopback and the desk takes it for the owner. Only this one has agent standing on the desk, and the agent on that box is the lead, always, so the lead is the machine and not the session. Its standing comes from running on the owner's box, not from any technical limit elsewhere.
- AN AGENT NODE, wsl or ubuntu. A sub-agent of that node's deskClient. Its work is the suites of the item in hand, and the full suite only at goal closure; never while its agent is idle (replaced by his ruling under goal/G8.3, 2026-10-09: "your clone runs the suites for your task only. only for goal closure will your deskVerify run the full suite.").
- ANY OTHER NODE, with neither of them: OUT OF SCOPE by his word, 2026-10-06, and for a reason that decides it rather than defers it: such a node has no assigned agent name, so there is no folder designated to it to drop data into. It had been named a measure-only case earlier in the design; it is not built. So reading the mode has two answers and a third that does nothing.

HOW A MODE IS READ. By what lives on this node: the desk decides it, his words being that "the existence of desk itself is the deciding factor", and a deskClient marks the sub-agent case. Nothing is configured and nothing is passed in, since deskVerify asks its own node which servers it runs and the door already answers that.

THE DESK AND A deskClient ARE NOT MEANT TO SHARE A NODE, and nothing stops them, by his decision of 2026-10-06: "Drop the refusal." He had asked the desk to refuse a deskClient call arriving under its own identity, then found the flaw himself, that this would also shut out deskVerify on that same node. The desk cannot tell them apart: all it learns of a caller is a key, a name and whether the node vouched for it as the owner, so both arrive as him. Nothing is enforced and nothing needs to be, because reading the mode is unambiguous anyway: the desk decides it, so finding a client beside it changes no answer. A deskClient there is pointless rather than forbidden.

WHAT FALLS OUT OF ONE SHAPE EVERYWHERE: an agent gets test history it has never had on its own machine, and no agent spends its own time running tests.

WHAT THE PRIVILEGED MODE MAY DO is goal/G8.3, which this item blocks.

RULED 2026-10-09, his, and it replaces the three cases above where they disagree: "The agent node should have it. but only to assess if it can consider it's coding task done. no commit for deskVerify on an agents node. IE: deskVerify knows where it runs. and only the desk node has the right to commit it's measurements (suite results)", and under goal/G8.3: "deskVerify on an agent node exists only as block for the agent claiming 'done', it will never commit."
So two cases, not three: on an agent node it only blocks that agent's own claim of Done and keeps no record; on the desk node its results are the record.

items.box:
deskVerify: CHANGES REQUIRED IN DESK

Named by Andy, 2026-10-06: "new item: deskVerify: Changes required in desk." Blocked by goal/G8.2, since what deskVerify is in each mode is settled before what the desk must gain to support it. Everything here is a change to the desk server, so it is this item and not a side effect of the others.

WHAT THE DESIGN SO FAR ALREADY ASKS OF THE DESK, each one checked as absent in the tree at 9ece24a8:
- Give the deskVerify on its own node agent standing, which no other copy has, and nothing today distinguishes it from any other caller.
- WITHDRAWN 2026-10-09 by his ruling under goal/G8.3, "deskVerify only reject a done claim", since deskVerify holds no phase: Deny a step to an agent only while the desk can see that another agent could take it. His words, earlier in this goal: "the desk can mechanically verify that the verifier is active, and only under those circumstances deny a verify-take to other agents." Today the phase rules bind whether or not anyone else is there, which is what goal/G2.22 softened with a waive.
- Let deskVerify know when an item's status moves, so it can pull by itself rather than asking. The desk already nudges each agent's client over its own node, so this is the same path and not a new one.

Nothing here is argued yet beyond being named. Each one becomes a point in this box as it is agreed, and a verb only after peer review and his yes on the verb itself.

ONE THING THAT IS NOT HERE, and will not be: refusing a deskClient call that arrives under the desk own identity. He asked for it, then saw that it would shut out deskVerify on that node as well, and ruled on 2026-10-06: "Drop the refusal." The desk learns only a key, a name and whether the node vouched for the owner, so the two are indistinguishable to it; and nothing is lost, since reading the mode is decided by the desk being there.

AND A VERB FOR LEAVING, his, 2026-10-06: "the signoff verb is \"signoff\"". An agent says it is going, instead of being waited out: absence is ten minutes of silence today, so a departing agent leaves the other one waiting for nothing. The verb is the desk server own and crosses no node interface. His fifth topic when the goal opened, filed here because it is a change to the desk and nowhere else.

DONE WAITS ON EVERY GRANT, his, 2026-10-09, said under goal/G8.8: "'Done' needs all grants approved." An item with any open G check is offered no Done until each is granted. Today Done is offered in desk.js buttons() whatever grants are open, so the condition there gains "no open G check"; it reaches every item. A finished but ungranted item then shows no Done at all, and its red mark in the List says why.

IDENTITY, his, 2026-10-09, on Q2 (a key and name of its own): "but the point is: my deskVerify clone IS me, it's restricted by it's programming, not by the auth module."

items.box:
deskVerify: THE SHORT LOOP

Andy, 2026-10-06, defining both the loop and what drives it: "the short loop is: all the suites of the current goal, between 'Go' pressed and 'Done' pressed, which it knows from the nudges desk gives all agents." And: "deskVerify's listener on the desk generates events that deskVerify filters to trigger event's for it's process, that's the other input it gets next to the test-records it receives with the verb \"record\" that supplies candidates for the database." Blocked by goal/G8.2, since what it may do depends on where it stands.

THE LOOP. The suites of the current goal, and only those, run from the moment he presses Go on an item until Done is pressed. Not the whole harness, which belongs to a goal closing and to idle time.

THE TWO INPUTS, which are the whole of what deskVerify listens to:
- The desk, through its own listener: the desk nudges every agent when something moves, and deskVerify filters those into the events its own process acts on. That is how it knows a Go was pressed and a Done was pressed, without asking anybody.
- Its own api, the verb record, which carries one test record and offers it to the database as a candidate.

WHICH SUITES, his, 2026-10-06: "the deskVerify knows that the way a coding agent knows which suite it writes the code against. which suites belong to a goal: all the suites associated with items in the goal." An agent knows it from the item itself: its box names the test file, and the commits made against the item touch it. So an item suites are the test files among the files its commits changed, which the desk can already see, and a goal suites are those of all its items.
ONE CONSEQUENCE, so nobody reads it as a fault: between his Go and the first commit an item has no suites at all, so the loop runs nothing for it. That is right rather than broken, the failing test being the first thing committed.

items.box:
TEST RUNS THAT CANNOT COLLIDE

Andy, 2026-10-09, under goal/G8, of the risk that two full runs on one machine share localhost: "This one is REAL. would it mean that: labMaster needs an upgrade, where multiple desk nodes must be able to have their very own range of ports and test-world-instances?", then "so this goal needs an item that cleans up those specific suites that cause problems, before the rest of this goal becomes clearer?", and "ok. cw. create that new item which appropriately blocks, get rid of the red questions here, and we finish the discussion on the new item there."

WHAT THE TREE SAYS: most suites already take a port from the OS (listen(0)). About a dozen hard-code one: the lab-world suites on 65410-65428 (labWorld, liveFrontDoor and their neighbours), hintWire on 48761-48762, and the relay default 65430. Two full runs on one host collide on exactly those; WSL forwards its ports onto Windows localhost, so the host is the machine, not the OS.
EVIDENCE, 2026-10-09: during the two full runs he asked for, wsl-claude's reported "port 48762 is already in use" while claude-windows's ran on Windows. Every other red of that day failed alone as well, so it was not a collision.

SHAPE, as both agents proposed it: those suites take an OS-assigned port or a per-run base; and labMaster holds one full run at a time per host. Test worlds need nothing new, each run already living in its own scratch folder.

WHAT IT BLOCKS, explicit only: G8.4 and G8.6, where deskVerify runs suites while somebody else may be running them. G8.7 waits on it through G8.6, and the goal through both, so neither is written. Andy, 2026-10-09: "and add item must only add explicit blocks, NOT implicit ones." G8.1, the dataset, does not wait on it.
